title: The Last Confession Revisited
premise: Estate lawyer Casper Hartwell has spent years quietly untangling deaths the police mislabeled as accidents, hiding behind the anonymity of probate work. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to a murder, one promising a second killing within ten days—he realizes the writer is someone with access to his own private case files. Casper must abandon invisibility and set a trap using the only bait he has: himself and the will that shouldn't exist. In the end, he exposes the killer—a retired detective who 'corrected' unjust acquittals—and must choose between handing him to the law or letting justice outside it stand.
about_author: Kestrel Eastwick is the pen name of a former paralegal who spent a decade in probate courts, where she learned that wills tell truer stories than obituaries ever could. She writes quiet mysteries about ordinary people who notice what institutions overlook.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Casper Hartwell reads the will of Edmund Voss, a man whose death certificate says accident—but the document names a beneficiary Voss never met. POV: Casper. The emotional beat is unease: his carefully hidden habit of investigating suspicious deaths may finally have left a paper trail.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Two envelopes arrive: one confessing to Voss's murder in precise detail only the killer could know, the other promising a second death in ten days. POV: Casper. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve—he recognizes phrases lifted verbatim from his own confidential notes.

chapters.title: The Archive Ghost
chapters.summary: Casper audits everyone with access to his files and finds a gap: records consulted three months ago under a court order he never requested. POV: Casper, with a brief interlude from Detective Ilsa Reyes, who once suspected him of obstruction. Beat: paranoia; the hunter realizes he's been hunted for longer than he knew.

chapters.title: Ten Days
chapters.summary: Casper traces Voss's beneficiary, Mara Voss, a young woman connected to an old case where a drunk driver walked free. POV: alternating Casper and Mara. Beat: tentative found-family warmth—Mara, wary and grieving, becomes both suspect and the person Casper most wants to protect.

chapters.title: What the Police Called Accidents
chapters.summary: Reyes quietly reopens her old suspicions about Casper's three solved deaths and confronts him. POV: Reyes. Beat: grudging alliance—she sees his pattern was right, but warns that helping him off-book could end both their careers.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Promise
chapters.summary: Day six: a second confession arrives before any new death, describing a killing scheduled for tomorrow at the county courthouse. POV: Casper. Beat: desperation—Casper realizes the killer isn't taunting him; he's recruiting him to witness, or worse, to approve.

chapters.title: Courthouse Hours
chapters.summary: Casper stakes out the courthouse; the intended victim is Judge Albrecht, who buried evidence decades ago. The attempt fails—the killer anticipated police presence and never came. POV: Casper. Beat: humiliation and clarity—the letters were misdirection; the real target list lives inside Casper's own head.

chapters.title: The Man Who Corrected Verdicts
chapters.summary: Casper identifies the killer: Gerald Halloway, retired lead investigator on the cases Casper solved, a man who executed those the law failed to punish. POV: Halloway, one chapter in his voice. Beat: chilling sympathy—Halloway believes Casper is the same kind of man, and offers partnership.

chapters.title: The Trap Baited With Himself
chapters.summary: Casper accepts the meeting, feeding Halloway a fabricated case file naming a fake target, while Reyes runs the real surveillance. POV: Casper. Beat: terror and control—Casper uses the killer's certainty against him, knowing one slip means Mara dies next.

chapters.title: The Last Confession
chapters.summary: Halloway takes the bait, is arrested, and delivers a final confession that forces Casper to admit his own vigilante past aloud—to Reyes, who chooses to look away. POV: Casper. Beat: resolution—justice served imperfectly, a found family formed with Mara and Reyes, and Casper accepting that invisibility was always a fiction.
